question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[1,2]\times [1,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)={x}^{4}+{y}^{4}-4{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}+10. $$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1,\,1]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[2,\,2]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**
${x}_{2}=[$ {{field-1}} $]$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4}+{y}^{4}-4{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}+10) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{4}+{y}^{4}-4{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}+10)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3}-8x \\ 4{y}^{3}-8y\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{x}^{3}-8x) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(4{y}^{3}-8y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{3}-8x) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(4{y}^{3}-8y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12{x}^{2}-8 & 0 \\ 0 & 12{y}^{2}-8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}12{x}^{2}-8 & 0 \\ 0 & 12{y}^{2}-8\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3}-8x \\ 4{y}^{3}-8y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}12{x}^{2}-8 & 0 \\ 0 & 12{y}^{2}-8\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3}-8x \\ 4{y}^{3}-8y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}12(2)^{2}-8 & 0 \\ 0 & 12(2)^{2}-8\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}4(2)^{3}-8(2) \\ 4(2)^{3}-8(2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}40 & 0 \\ 0 & 40\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}16 \\ 16\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{40\cdot 40-0\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}40 & 0 \\ 0 & 40\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}16 \\ 16\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{1\,600}[\begin{aligned}640 \\ 640\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.6 \\ 1.6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
